newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Lebed has been favourite target of Russia's elite.
newsitem.headline: Lebed has been favourite target of Russia's elite.

text.p: Russian security chief Alexander Lebed, accused of plotting to seize power, is no stranger to controversy and has made many enemies since blazing his way into the Kremlin just three months ago.

Interior Minister Anatoly Kulikov, who said the gruff reserve general was staging a "creeping coup" as President Boris Yeltsin waited for heart surgery, is a much less colourful figure, but he has emerged as Lebed's most public critic.
Here are some of the comments made by and about Lebed as members Yeltsin's entourage maneouvre for position while the president is away.
--Kulikov on Lebed:
"(Lebed) has decided to move ahead using force instead of waiting for the next presidential poll...

"He is actively using his authority as Security Council secretary to create power structures reporting personally to him. The question is what awaits Russia if Lebed comes to power through a creeping coup."
Lebed's peace deal for Chechnya was - "a cover for the most humiliating unilateral concessions".
--Lebed on Kulikov:
On Wednesday - "There can be no talk of a mutiny." Asked to explain Kulikov's charges, he added: "The poor thing has got everything wrong."

In August - "Now I address Russian President Boris Nikolayevich Yeltsin: you will have to make a difficult choice. Only one must stay -- Lebed or Kulikov...Otherwise, everything will deteriorate into a fight with a man obsessed with a Napoleon complex."
--Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin on the conflict:
"I do not conceal my concern over the fact that a considerable part of what Minister Kulikov said corresponds with reality... (I am) far from thinking about mutinies and putsches"
--Yeltsin chief-of-staff Anatoly Chubais on Lebed:
"We can always turn on the television and find out what Alexander Ivanovich (Lebed) has done recently and what he's planning to do next."
--Moscow mayor Yuri Luzhkov, a likely rival in any future presidential race, on Lebed:
"I do not understand, what moral right does a person who willingly agreed to work in the president's team have to declare his ambitions for power now?"
--Yeltsin on Lebed
"He (Lebed) needs to get down to business now, carry out the tasks he already has and make more effort to work with the premier and with the other services.
"You can't quarrel with everyone all the time. You can't settle issues that way. Our state apparatus must live in peace."
--Lebed on himself
"I was a born winner. Sooner or later, victory will be mine."
"Somebody really wants me to break my neck in tackling the Chechen crisis. We'll see. I like tough tasks."
